messages:
arjun: Heads-up — saw a nasty 150-220ms stall on a single request during KV warmup in the nsys trace. Looks like matmul algo re-selection + workspace mallocs spike right when the prefetch kicks in. attaching short nsys snippet.

arjun: ```
nsys timeline: [0.00s..0.35s]
  cpu: prefetch_kv_batch (18ms)
  gpu: gemmLtAlgoSelect (0.12s) -> sgemm_kernel (0.05s) -> cudaMalloc (0.07s)
  note: repeated small cudaMalloc/free in between kernels
```

lisa: ugh, shape? batch size? was this on a 1-step or long chat request?

arjun: short request (1 token generation). shapes: B=1, S=128, hidden=4096 -> matmul A: [1,128,4096], B: [4096,1024] (so big workspace). Trigger seems correlated with KV prefetch which runs a small dense matmuls to merge cached prefix.

mike: that pattern screams workspace pressure + fragmentation. If cuBLASLt probes during runtime it'll pick an algo that needs a large workspace; then our runtime tries to alloc slab and that forces small cudaMallocs -> stalls. Could also be that prefetch runs several matmuls back-to-back and causes temporary high peak.

sophia: do we have the cublasLt heuristic trace? I want to see if it chose algo with workspace > free slab. Also check if prefetch is using our 'prefetch_async' path vs serial path. Async prefetch can overlap but still needs workspace.

arjun: here's the cublasLt log snippet I captured:```
[cublasLt] algo_select: algo_id=7, workspace=7864320, time_est=0.048s
[cublasLt] fallback: algo_id=2, workspace=0, time_est=0.055s
```

lisa: interesting — algo 7 needs ~7.5MB. Our per-GPU slab free window was around 4MB at that moment (from perfetto memory track). So it tried algo 7, failed to get slab, then triggered cudaMallocs and fell back, but the probe itself caused the bad allocation pattern.

mike: two short repros to try: (1) run the same workload with prefetch disabled, (2) force cublasLt to avoid workspace-heavy algos (env override) to see if stall goes away. I can run both on qgpu-07.

sophia: if repro is stable we should consider a short-term runtime guard: when prefetch is about to run and slab free < X, force prefetch to pick no-ws algos or defer prefetch. Also longer-term: pre-reserve scratch pool for cuBLASLt probes to avoid fragmentation.

arjun: did a quick test locally: disabled prefetch -> median latency drops 170ms -> tail improves a lot. So prefetch + probe is the culprit.

mike: ran the env override test: `export RW_CUBLASLT_MAX_WORKSPACE=0` (internal helper) -> same improvement. So two mitigation paths validated.

lisa: awesome. let's open a small perf ticket + a canary config. If we gate prefetch with a cheap slab-check that should be low risk.

perf-bot: Created PERF-3456: "kv-prefetch: guard cuBLASLt algoprobes when slab low" assigned to @mike, priority P2. <https://tickets.internal/PERF-3456> :white_check_mark:

mike: plan: patch runtime to check slab_free_bytes() > RW_CUBLASLT_PROBE_THRESHOLD (default 16MB) before running prefetch probing; if not, pick deterministic no-ws algo. Will add a flag to force probe for Dedicated customers. I'll draft PR.

sophia: also add a small nsys perf-test in CI: run short sequence with prefetch on/off and assert tail < +50ms. Helps catch regressions.

arjun: thanks — re-ran perfetto after disabling probe and the memory timeline is much cleaner (no malloc spikes). attaching screenshot in thread.

lisa: p.s. can we add a telemetry metric (probe-caused-mallocs) so we can alert if this spikes? would help customers on Dedicated.

mike: yep, will emit an event on probe path if we fall back to cudaMallocs during probe. good signal.

sophia: linking related notes in the ticket: kernel timeline, sample nsys + perfetto snippets, and suggested slab threshold.

arjun: thanks team — leaving the traces in PERF-3456. next step: PR + canary on qgpu-07 with perf tests.

lisa: :thumbsup:
